authority: Crother, White, Savage, Eckstut, Graham & Gardner, 2011

diet.text: Mainly mice and other small rodents

overview.text: The Western Fox Snake is a harmless rat snake of the upper Midwest of the United States, west of the Mississippi River. It was named as a separate species in 2011.

distribution.label: Native
distribution.text: West of the Mississippi in south-eastern Minnesota, Iowa, south-eastern South Dakota, eastern Nebraska and northern Missouri.

habitat.text: Forest, shrubland, grassland and wetlands, and also pasture, old fields and farmland.

behaviour.text: Fairly bold. When confronted it shakes its tail like a rattlesnake, takes an S-shaped pose and snaps.

diet.text: A constrictor that eats mainly mice and other small rodents, plus young rabbits, frogs and eggs.

reproduction.text: Lays eggs in rotting stumps and under logs.

recognise.text: Shakes its tail like a rattlesnake but has no rattle.
